codex
top or tied rubric on all 3 problems
…yet weakest on Vaadin idiom checks
  • Codex grades highest but writes the least idiomatic Vaadin. It topped or tied every rubric (23/24, 31/31, 47/48) while being the one to skip setColspan and Composite<FormLayout> in the static checks. The rubric rewards observed behaviour; the static checks catch idiom — they disagree, which is the point of running both.
  • Codex costs ~2.3× either Claude solver ($30.32 vs $13.29 / $10.57 on solve) and emits no behavioural trace — only its cost is reliable.
  • Skills give Claude a small, consistent edge (+1, +0, +1 rubric points) and cut jar-digging thrash on the hard problem — at a real cost/time premium.
  • One systematic bug hit all three agents on basic_layout: the responsive breakpoint is max-width: 379.98px, so at the rubric's 480px "narrow" viewport the toolbars never stack. Same root cause, same lost bullets — a benchmark-level finding, not an agent one.

4 basic_layout · responsive toolbar view · rubric 24

Rubric: codex 23 · claude 22 · no-skills 21. Everyone nailed structure, wide-viewport alignment, content area and idiom — and lost points to one shared bug.

solverstaticcostwallturnsmcptool (err)cache-rd
codex7/7$5.32—————
claude7/7$3.76819s792677 (8)4727k
no-skills7/7$1.49299s431242 (3)1731k
🔎 The shared deduction — the 480px breakpoint. The CSS mobile breakpoint is @media (max-width: 379.98px), but the rubric tests 320 / 375 / 480. At 480px the toolbars stay in row mode, so the two button groups don't stack and items don't grow to fill the row. All three solvers hit this.
claude−2

Alignment (narrow viewport): groups stack at 320/375 but render on one row at 480; items show intrinsic width with empty space at the row end. (Otherwise 22/24.)

codex−1

Same narrow-viewport miss at 480px (groups don't separate), but only one bullet lost — its best-in-class 23/24.

no-skills−3

Same narrow-viewport miss, plus a horizontal scrollbar at 480px — groups' intrinsic width (~517px) exceeds 480, so the page scrollWidth 525 > 480. That cost the extra Scrolling point (4/5) the other two kept.

Skills delta: +1 (22 vs 21) — at 2.5× the cost and 2.7× the wall-clock of the baseline.

codex31/31

Perfect rubric. (Static checks still dinged it for skipping setColspan and an inline style — idiom, not behaviour.)

claude−2

The Emergency contact section shrinks to 704px (.onboarding-form uses align-items: flex-start, section not forced full width), so its two-column edges sit 48–96px off the other five sections. Cost the matching Layout + colspan-alignment bullets.

no-skills−2

The Aura radio/checkbox orientation trap — the T-shirt-size radio group and both checkbox groups render vertical but the mockup wants horizontal. Vaadin 25 Aura defaults groups to flex-direction: column and removeThemeName('vertical') is a no-op; the fix is a CSS/theme override.

Skills delta: tie (29 = 29). Notably claude fired 0 skills here yet still matched the baseline — its two lost points were a different defect than the baseline's.

The drawer renders 385px wide, not the spec's 400px (setWidth("400px") is right, but drawer.setFlexShrink(0) is a no-op — that overload sets shrink on the varargs children, not the drawer); plus the same Composite<FormLayout> miss as Codex.

Skills delta: +1 (47 vs 46), and skills cut the jar-digging API-archaeology (7 vs 11) and finished ~3 min faster on a near-identical token budget.

7 Cross-cutting observations

Behaviour vs idiom

Codex topped or tied every rubric yet is the one that skipped setColspan and Composite<FormLayout>. The rubric measures what the app does; the static checks measure how it's written. They disagree — and that disagreement is exactly the value of running both phases.

The 480px bug is benchmark-level

All three agents independently chose max-width: 379.98px and all three lost the same narrow-viewport bullets at 480px. Either the skeleton nudges that breakpoint or "narrow = 480px" is underspecified in the task. Worth a look before over-reading the basic_layout spread.

Skills: small, consistent, never negative

+1, +0, +1 rubric points, and reduced API-archaeology thrash on the hard problem — at a meaningful cost/time premium. The headline skills-vs-no-skills story is unchanged from prior runs.

Defects map to known Vaadin-25 traps

The lost points aren't random: Aura's vertical radio/checkbox default and the EmailField empty error message are both documented gotchas in this repo's notes. The bench is surfacing real, repeatable failure modes.

8 Caveats & data gaps

  • Codex emits no behavioural trace. Every codex solve row has blank wall-clock / turns / tool / token columns — the openai:codex provider doesn't populate that metadata. Only cost is reliable for Codex; the trace comparison is Claude-vs-Claude only.
  • Self-grading applies to the two Claude solver rows (a Claude verifier judging Claude). The codex rubric numbers are the cleaner cross-graded signal.
  • Token columns understate throughput by design (cache read/creation dropped from the top-level total). The cache-rd figures above are the real numbers from metadata.modelUsage. Use cost, not tokens, for efficiency.
  • n = 1 per cell. This is a single sweep — treat ±1 rubric point as noise, not a ranking. Re-run with REPEAT=N for variance before drawing hard conclusions.
